alignments.note: Rule 32 with rule 31's verbless-modifier carve-out: the substantival article supplies the pronoun, and since its modifier is a prepositional phrase with no verb it keeps the relativizer too; discontinuous under rule 15.
Ordinary negator; no negative indefinite follows.

Predicate noun with its supplied indefinite determiner; rule 103's contrast folds the resumptive pro-form *one* onto the token it resumes, discontinuously under rule 15. Marking *one* added remains defensible.
Rule 93: the article contributes no part of the fused English adverb.

Rule 94: the ASV renders the prepositional phrase by the single word *outwardly*, with a supplied copula riding along under rule 53; part of that word answers to φανερῷ, so rule 39 keeps it aligned, headed on the governed word.
Rule 31: an article preceding its expressed noun takes the determiner along with the supplied relativizer; rule 60 makes the supplied demonstrative the article's own, headed on it.
Rules 53 and 63: the clause is verbless, so the predicate noun carries the supplied copula, discontinuously under rule 15.
Rule 93: the second article likewise contributes nothing.
Rule 94 with rule 53, as at the first occurrence; the ASV writes the adjectival *outward* here and the adverbial *outwardly* above, which rule 24 treats as one analysis.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause: the supplied determiner belongs to the noun.

review_notes: Both ἐν τῷ φανερῷ phrases are analysed alike under rules 93 and 94, the article empty and the preposition joined to the adjective.
*one* at t009 is folded onto Ἰουδαῖος as a resumptive pro-form under rule 103's stated contrast rather than marked added.
